entry.title: Debate 278: John Lennox vs Michael Tooley — Atheism and Christianity · 2013
entry.summary: Tooley wins by separating atheism from anti-Christian critique and pressing evil and prophecy; Lennox offers strong compatibility replies but leaves key positive warrants underdeveloped.

entry.title: Debate 277: Michael Shermer vs Glen Scrivener — Can We Be Good Without God? · 2024
entry.summary: Scrivener narrowly wins by pressing universal human worth and outsider scope, while Shermer offers strong fallibilist reasons but leaves equal rights incompletely grounded.

entry.title: Debate 276: Randal Rauser vs Aron Ra — Biblical Violence and Divine Revelation · 2022
entry.summary: Rauser won by offering a morally constrained, genre-sensitive, fallibilist account of revelation, while Aron's strongest internal critiques exposed unresolved evidential and doctrinal costs.

entry.title: Debate 275: William Lane Craig vs Michael Tooley — Is God Real? · 2010
entry.summary: Craig’s cumulative theistic case confronts Tooley’s probabilistic evil argument, with moral perfection and inductive method ultimately deciding a narrowly stronger con case.

entry.title: Debate 274: Eli Ayala vs Dan Barker — Does the God of the Bible Exist? · 2026
entry.summary: Barker won by exposing the gap between transcendental theism and the biblical God, while Ayala effectively qualified prayer claims and challenged Barker's moral foundation.

entry.title: Debate 273: William Lane Craig vs Austin Dacey — Does God Exist? · 2004
entry.summary: Dacey won by sustaining stronger comparative cases from hiddenness, suffering, embodied minds, and evolution while repeatedly undercutting Craig’s central explanatory bridges.

entry.title: Debate 272: Jonathan McLatchie vs Tom Jump — Does God Exist? · 2019
entry.summary: McLatchie’s cumulative Bayesian case narrowly prevailed, while Jump’s underdetermination challenges exposed unresolved comparisons behind its numerical confidence.

entry.title: Debate 271: William Lane Craig vs Massimo Pigliucci — Does the Christian God Exist? · 2001
entry.summary: Craig prevailed through cumulative structure, sharper historical replies, and key conceptual distinctions, while Pigliucci led on scope and pressed serious evidential alternatives.

entry.title: Debate 270: Trent Horn vs Dan Barker — Does the Christian God Exist? · 2018
entry.summary: Horn narrowly prevailed through stronger metaphysical replies and a resilient resurrection case, while Barker excelled on institutional accountability, scriptural morality, and textual conflict.

entry.title: Debate 269: Andrew Loke vs Dan Linford — Physical Reality, Causation, and Beginnings · 2023
entry.summary: Linford’s carefully limited skepticism outperformed Loke’s positive case by separating first changes from total beginnings and sustaining nonmetric, timeless-grounding, and material-parity alternatives.

entry.title: Debate 268: Jonathan Sacks vs Richard Dawkins — Science and Religion · 2012
entry.summary: Sacks defends compatibility through distinct roles and disciplined interpretation, while Dawkins more successfully presses whether religious purpose and supernatural premises have independent warrant.

entry.title: Debate 267: Christopher Hitchens vs Douglas Wilson — Truth, Goodness, and Beauty · 2008
entry.summary: Wilson argues that theism grounds reason, value, and purposeful beauty; Hitchens answers with human responsibility, secular awe, skeptical inquiry, and stricter tests for miracles.

entry.title: Debate 266: Matt Dillahunty vs Blake Giunta — Faith and Rational Justification · 2018
entry.summary: A closely matched exchange tests whether theism needs prior possibility evidence or may enter ordinary comparative inference, with Dillahunty prevailing by one point.

entry.title: Debate 265: Miles K. Donahue vs Dan Linford — Fine-Tuning and Theism · 2026
entry.summary: Linford’s measure and model-flexibility objections outperformed Donahue’s modest fine-tuning case, whose strongest distinctions remained burdened by unsupported probability assignments.

entry.title: Debate 264: Deepak Chopra vs Richard Dawkins — Consciousness, Cosmic Purpose, and Spirituality · 2013
entry.summary: Dawkins wins through scale-sensitive emergence arguments and precise criticism of quantum equivocation; Chopra’s strongest reply challenges confidence in promised brain-only explanation.

entry.title: Debate 263: William Dembski vs Christopher Hitchens — Does a good God exist? · 2010
entry.summary: Hitchens wins by exposing the gap between design and a good providential God, while Dembski offers careful limits and several effective scientific replies.

entry.title: Debate 262: Sam Harris vs Jonathan Haidt — Religion, moral truth, and human flourishing · 2016
entry.summary: Two naturalists contest whether broad well-being can ground moral truth, with Harris strongest on scope and Haidt strongest on psychology, institutions, and plural goods.

entry.title: Debate 261: Al Sharpton vs Christopher Hitchens — God, religion, and morality · 2007
entry.summary: Sharpton narrowed the case to personal theism, but Hitchens won by separating private belief from public warrant and supplying stronger naturalistic alternatives.

entry.title: Debate 260: Shmuley Boteach vs Christopher Hitchens — God and morality · 2008
entry.summary: Boteach grounds design and human worth in a personal God; Hitchens answers with natural explanation, moral autonomy, and challenges to interventionist religion.

entry.title: Debate 259: Bernardo Kastrup vs Susan Blackmore — Consciousness and illusion · 2023
entry.summary: Blackmore’s disciplined challenges expose gaps in Kastrup’s elegant idealist account, especially around boundaries and evidence, while her limited method avoids claiming a rival metaphysics.

entry.title: Debate 258: James White vs Robert Price — Is the Bible true? · 2010
entry.summary: White narrowly wins through manuscript-stream and contextual replies, while Price’s strongest challenges expose methodological limits, oral flexibility, and inerrancy’s interpretive costs.

entry.title: Debate 257: Peter Atkins vs Stephen Law — Science or philosophy? · 2014
entry.summary: Atkins champions evidence-driven scientific expansion; Law concedes science’s empirical authority while defending conceptual analysis, ultimate explanation, and moral justification as indispensable.

entry.title: Debate 256: Aron Ra vs Michael Jones — Is Christianity dangerous? · 2019
entry.summary: Aron documents scriptural and social harms, but Jones wins by repeatedly separating Christian identity from causation and challenging unadjusted comparisons.

entry.title: Debate 255: Mike Licona vs Richard Carrier — Did Jesus rise from the dead? · 2004
entry.summary: Licona narrowly prevails through cumulative historical breadth, while Carrier’s Pauline, visionary, source-critical, and prior-probability challenges keep every decisive inference closely contested.

entry.title: Debate 254: Cliffe Knechtle & Stuart Knechtle vs Matt Dillahunty & Joshua Bowen: Is the Bible's treatment of slavery morally defensible? · 2021
entry.summary: The critics prevail by grounding ownership and coercion in specific texts, while the defenders’ canonical trajectory never fully reconciles those legal permissions.
